chunks: Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: My father said: 'Verily, a man fasts one day voluntarily, seeking what is in the presence of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and Allah enters him into Paradise through it.'

key_terms.الْجَنَّةَ: Paradise (al-Janna) — the abode of reward and eternal bliss in the hereafter
key_terms.تَطَوُّعاً: voluntary/supererogatory act — an act of worship beyond what is obligatory (fard), performed for extra merit
key_terms.مَا عِنْدَ اللَّهِ: what is in the presence of Allah — divine reward and nearness to God in the afterlife

ai.seo_question: What is the reward for fasting one day voluntarily according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (a.s.) reports from his father Imam al-Baqir (a.s.) that a single voluntary fast performed with sincere intention for Allah's sake is sufficient to earn a person entry into Paradise. This teaching emphasizes the immense spiritual value of nawafil (supererogatory) acts of worship, particularly voluntary fasting (sawm al-tatawwu'), and encourages believers to perform additional acts of devotion beyond what is obligatory. The original audience of Shia Muslims would have understood 'what is in the presence of Allah' (ma 'inda Allah) as a reference to divine reward and nearness to God, a concept central to Quranic piety.
